newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt paper mkt price rise seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt paper mkt price rise seen.

text.p: Russia's decision on Monday to cut the guaranteed dollar yield for foreigners on domestic government paper will have little impact on the market, dealers said, forecasting a slight price rise on Tuesday.
*Average yield rose to 18.36 pct from 18.06 pct on Friday
*Turnover fell to 2.06 trln rbls from 3.81 trln rbls

Dealers said yields would edge down smoothly in line with central bank policy. The central bank is seen making the move gradual in order to cushion commercial banks from the shock of lower T-bill profits.
"A period of stability has emerged on the market, " said Aljba-Alliance Bank dealer Mikhail Vasilyev.
"Favourable economic and political events, especially the possibility for an improved credit rating for Russia in autumn, allows us to count for a smooth price rising trend."
He forecast a fall in the yields of long-term paper to 17 percent within the next two or three months. The current yield on long-term paper is around 18 percent.
The central bank announced a cut in non-resident yield guaranteed dollar yield to nine percent from 11 percent from July 15 but the move was not seen affecting prices.
The yield is guaranteed through forward contracts but the decision only affects paper maturing before the end of the year, when the market will be substantially liberalised for foreign investors.
"There are fewer than five months left until the end of the year and very few non-residents want to invest for five months," Vasilyev said. "If they invest money at all, it is for a year, or two."
